TELEX / DOCUMENTATION

A little guidance.
Then you’re on.

Your guide to scripts, pacing and your next great take.

01

Getting started

Telex is a native macOS teleprompter for macOS 14 or later, with Apple silicon and Intel binaries. Download the development build from GitHub Releases. It is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS may block opening it.

Review the app’s terms on first launch. For prompting without permissions, choose No microphone in Pacing. The current app defaults to Voice level; it asks for microphone access when you explicitly activate reading or the microphone test.

02

Bring your words

Create a script in the editor, paste your text, or use Import script for a UTF-8 .txt or .md file. RTF import/export is also supported. Draft changes are saved locally. Rename, duplicate, search or export a script from the workspace.

Editing stops prompting so your microphone and overlay are not left running while you type. Each script supports up to 500,000 Swift characters.

03

Choose your pace

No microphone

Continuous scrolling works without microphone, camera or Speech permission. Start, pause, resume, restart or return to the top. Set a countdown or change speed while reading.

The current development presets are Very slow 40, Slow 80, Medium 130, Medium fast 180, High 240 and Very high 300 WPM. These are target speeds based on estimated text layout, not a measured speaking-speed guarantee.

Voice level

Microphone input determines when scrolling advances. When speaking stops, scrolling holds. Set Mic sensitivity below your normal speaking level while keeping it above background noise. The Input level meter is a display, not a slider.

Script words (optional)

Apple on-device transcription can align speech with your script. It requires separate Speech authorization and a supported language with available speech assets. If unavailable, the app explains the fallback to Voice level. There is no network recognition fallback.

Plain trackpad/wheel scrolling and cue jumps remain available. A separate Manual mode and camera recording mode are not yet implemented.

04

Find the right cue

Put a heading on its own line, before its section. Use a normal space after the #:

# Opening
Welcome, everyone.

# The big idea
Here is what we are building.

# Next steps
Let’s talk about what comes next.

You can also use [Cue: Next steps] on its own line. Cue titles appear visibly in the prompter. They are not hidden timing or pause commands. Click a cue to jump and use Return to spot to go back.

05

A few handy shortcuts

Current application shortcuts
ActionShortcut
Play / pause⌘ Return
Show / hide⇧ ⌘ T
Dock / float⇧ ⌘ D
Toggle click-through⇧ ⌘ L
Screen recording controls⇧ ⌘ R
Faster / slower⌥ ⌘ + / −
Next / previous cue⌃ ⌥ → / ←
Return to spot⌃ ⌥ B
Fine scroll up / down⌥ ⌘ ↑ / ↓

Other apps can own these shortcuts. Telex shows a conflict warning and offers retry. Use workspace or menu controls if a shortcut is unavailable.

06

Permissions stay separate

No-microphone prompting needs no capture permissions. Voice pacing uses the microphone; optional transcription also needs Speech permission. Screen recording is a separate, optional action with its own permission. Recording audio is separately opt-in.

Stealth is best effort and Limited on macOS 15 or later. Third-party display sharing may include the panel. Share an application window, use another display or hide the panel. Always check a test recording. macOS privacy indicators cannot be hidden.

07

Find your flow again

The script does not move when I speak

Move the pointer off the panel if hover pause is enabled, unlock a manual pause and check the countdown. Test the microphone. If the input meter is below your sensitivity threshold, speak normally and use Adjust sensitivity from my voice. No-microphone mode provides continuous scrolling without speech permissions.

I cannot click the panel

Turn off Click-through with ⇧⌘L or from the menu bar. The inspector also has a Turn off click-through button. Click-through intentionally prevents clicks and hover from reaching the overlay.

Word following is unavailable

Check the language and permission notice. You do not have to enable Siri or Apple Speech to use Voice level or No microphone. Transcription accuracy and availability vary with system assets and language.

08

Development, honestly

The published development build has 54 passing tests in Xcode and Swift package runs, plus passing Xcode analysis. The geometry cycling regression was fixed. Live microphone meter movement has been confirmed.

These are scoped results. Live word-following accuracy, third-party capture behavior, interrupted recording recovery, full accessibility and sustained performance checks remain incomplete. The build has not passed Developer ID signing, notarization or Gatekeeper release assessment.

The project is open source under the MIT license. View the source or check release notes and downloads.
